overview.mechanism: Inhibits DPP-4 and enhances endogenous incretin activity to improve glucose regulation.
uses: Glucose-lowering therapy for type 2 diabetes, including populations studied with reduced kidney function.

paragraphs.text: A renal pharmacokinetic study found modest exposure increases across impairment groups; less than 4% of the administered dose was removed during four-hour hemodialysis. These are study observations, not a substitute for the locally approved regimen.

The 132-participant GUARD trial reported improved glycemic control over 12 weeks in moderate-to-severe renal impairment. Albuminuria findings were secondary and do not prove prevention of kidney failure or establish long-term dialysis safety.

sources.citation: Shon et al. Effect of renal impairment and haemodialysis on the pharmacokinetics of gemigliptin. Diabetes Obes Metab. 2014;16:1028–1031. PubMed PMID: 24641348.
Efficacy, safety and albuminuria-reducing effect of gemigliptin in moderate to severe renal impairment: the GUARD Study. PubMed PMID: 28019072.
